findings.reason: as written §5's "bind with `unknown-unvalidated`, replace in §6" has no representation in the signal-map schema, and the landed maps already force identity (`channel_factor: 1.0`) on signed quantities, which is exactly the "forced rather than measured" outcome §6's own text forbids; the plan must state where an unvalidated signal-map sign is held (a new schema field, or the binding recorded as blocked until §6 measures it) instead of naming a field that schema does not own.
findings.text: the plan's §5 ("the magnetics bindings written, with sign_convention: unknown-unvalidated on every signed quantity until §6 replaces it"), §6 ("an emit path that lets a description binding whose sense §6 has now measured stop being unknown-unvalidated"; "sign_convention: unknown-unvalidated on every signed quantity, as §5 does for magnetics" for the FAME equilibrium signal map), and §8 ("replace every unknown-unvalidated that the data settles") all specify `sign_convention` on the pulse/equilibrium signal maps, but the signal-map schema has no such field: `SignalRule` (signal_map.py:95, `validate` at :146) requires `unit_factor` and `channel_factor` finite and nonzero, and its only sign carrier is the numeric `channel_factor` (`static_scale = unit_factor * channel_factor * convention_factor`, :118); `sign_convention` exists only on `ChannelBinding` (machine_map.py:147, legal values `_SIGN_CONVENTIONS` at :27 including `unknown-unvalidated`), which the transform engine applies (transform_engine.py:396 `_apply_sign_convention`). The landed maps confirm the divergence and its consequence: no map under imas_ambix/data/maps/ carries a `sign_convention` key, MAST carries sign numerically (`imas_ambix/data/maps/mast/*.json` `channel_factor: -1.0`), and the JT-60SA pulse maps fold the unvalidated sign to `channel_factor: 1.0` with the caveat only in the `evidence` string (`imas_ambix/data/maps/jt-60sa/magnetics.json`, `pf_active.json`, `tf.json` — every signed row), i.e. an assumed identity — the same instance appears again for the §6 FAME equilibrium map.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no new module; it extends existing owners, and each new public reader (`read_catalogue_observation`, `measure_convention`) hides a store read plus a typed-record adaptation behind one call rather than spreading behaviour across wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the sign-convention vocabulary is owned by machine_map.py `ChannelBinding` (where `unknown-unvalidated` is the only legal spelling), but the plan specifies `sign_convention: unknown-unvalidated` on pulse signal-map bindings, whose schema (`signal_map.py SignalRule`) has no such field and requires a finite nonzero `channel_factor`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section that adds surface names what it retires or why nothing can be (§2 exporter "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §6 "retires nothing, because no catalogue-driven observation reader exists" and "no equilibrium-database request type exists"; §7 retires three pinned constants and their re-export for one machine-keyed table; §5 "adds one data file and no public definition or refusal family").
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the owner it extends for every mechanism it adds and every citation checked out (transform_engine.py `_apply_cocos_convention`/`_apply_sign_convention`, cocos.py `canonical_factor`, cocos_convention.py `score_convention`/`read_level2_observation`, challenge/convention.py `measure_diiid_convention`, eval/efit_referee.py `GeometryVerdict`, gs/artifact_resolution.py `PINNED_*`, gs/machine_identity.py `default_registry`, spine_bench/runner.py `_magnetics_residual`), and no un-cited existing mechanism was found that does what a proposed one adds.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one sibling layer is justified and shares its computation: `read_level2_observation` keeps its MAST reads because MAST's catalogue binds no level-2 leaf, while the extracted kernel in cocos_convention.py is the single observation computation both readers call, so no thin re-export is added.
